newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaireans mob hotel to see "Angolan" boy soldiers.
newsitem.headline: Zaireans mob hotel to see "Angolan" boy soldiers.

text.p: Curious residents besieged a hotel in Zaire's mining capital Lubumbashi on Wednesday as word spread that Angolan boy soldiers were in town after deserting the frontline of Zaire's civil war.
"Look, they're tiny," said one man as a beaten-up yellow taxi, with polythene for a back window, rattled away with its young passengers from the Hotel Cosmopolite.

Rumour had it that two of the passengers, one looking no older than 12, were boy soldiers from Angola's former rebel force UNITA who had come across the border to help the beleaguered army of an old ally, President Mobutu Sese Seko.
Witnesses who sneaked into the hotel, past Zairean troops and secret police, said there were two more men under guard inside, chatting away in Angola's main language Portuguese.
All were in civilian clothes, though one carried a gun.
The taxi driver, who said his passengers also spoke Portuguese, deposited them into the care of the military at Civil Guard headquarters.
Townsfolk who gathered to see the newcomers said they had heard they had fled in front of rebels at Kasenga, some 220 km northeast of Lubumbashi.
Part of the cause for the great interest and carnival atmosphere was the belief the Angolans had some magic powers.
Zairean officials have accused Angola's government of sending troops to aid rebels led by Laurent Kabila, who have taken a quarter of Zaire since October.
The rebels in turn accuse UNITA of aiding Mobutu.

The United Nations, overseeing a 1994 peace agreement in Angola to end 19 years of civil war, said UNITA troops were backing Mobutu in a bid to keep open routes for its diamond trade and supplies from Zaire to its bases in northern and central Angola.
A U.N. official, who declined to be named, told Reuters recently about 2,000 UNITA troops had been flown out of two bases in Angola to Zaire to back government troops.
Diplomatic sources in Luanda said however that UNITA involvement in the fighting had recently stopped because the Angolans were suffering too many casualties.
Diplomats said Angolan government soldiers were backing the rebels to assist the Zairean rebels amid hopes of cutting off the UNITA supplies.
Washington has expressed concern at Angolan involvement in Zaire but has not being specific in its statements.

UNITA, with its northern stronghold along Zaire's border, had close ties with Mobutu through the Angolan war. It was widely believed to be involved in smuggling diamonds through Zaire to finance its struggle.
